title: Greeting, Paul's Desire to Visit Rome, The Righteous Shall Live by Faith, God's Wrath on Unrighteousness

questions.question: Paul introduces himself as a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle. What does he say he is set apart for?
options: The gospel of God
The ministry to the Gentiles
The defense of the truth
The teaching of the churches
questions.explanation: Romans 1:1 (ESV): "Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,"

questions.question: Concerning God's Son, Paul says he was descended from David according to the flesh, and was declared to be the Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness by what?
options: His resurrection from the dead
The miracles he performed
The voice of the Father at his baptism
His ascension to the right hand of God
questions.explanation: Romans 1:4 (ESV): "and was declared to be the Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness by his resurrection from the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,"

questions.question: Through Christ, Paul says they have received grace and apostleship to bring about what among all the nations?
options: The obedience of faith
The knowledge of salvation
The turning from idols
The collection for the saints
questions.explanation: Romans 1:5 (ESV): "through whom we have received grace and apostleship to bring about the obedience of faith for the sake of his name among all the nations,"

questions.question: For what reason does Paul thank God through Jesus Christ for all the believers in Rome?
options: Because their faith is proclaimed in all the world
Because they have remained faithful under persecution
Because of their generous gifts to the Jerusalem church
Because they have rejected the false teachers among them
questions.correctAnswer: Because their faith is proclaimed in all the world
questions.explanation: Romans 1:8 (ESV): "First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is proclaimed in all the world."

questions.question: Why does Paul say he longs to see the Roman believers?
options: That he may impart to them some spiritual gift to strengthen them
That he might collect an offering for the saints in Judea
That they might send him on his journey to Spain
That he might correct the divisions between Jews and Greeks
questions.correctAnswer: That he may impart to them some spiritual gift to strengthen them
questions.explanation: Romans 1:11 (ESV): "For I long to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you—"

questions.question: Paul says he is under obligation both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish. Therefore he is eager to do what?
options: Preach the gospel to those who are in Rome also
Suffer anything for the sake of the elect
Defend the gospel before Caesar himself
Write this letter to impart the truth before he arrives
questions.correctAnswer: Preach the gospel to those who are in Rome also
questions.explanation: Romans 1:14-15 (ESV): "I am under obligation both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish. So I am eager to preach the gospel to you also who are in Rome."

questions.question: Paul declares he is not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to whom?
options: The Greek
The Roman
The Gentile
The barbarian
questions.explanation: Romans 1:16 (ESV): "For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek."

questions.question: In the gospel, the righteousness of God is revealed from faith for faith, as it is written: "The righteous shall ____".
options: live by faith
inherit the earth
be saved
see God
questions.explanation: Romans 1:17 (ESV): "For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith for faith, as it is written, 'The righteous shall live by faith.'"

questions.question: The wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who by their unrighteousness do what?
options: Suppress the truth
Mock God's law
Persecute the righteous
Deny the Creator
questions.explanation: Romans 1:18 (ESV): "For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who by their unrighteousness suppress the truth."

questions.question: What can be clearly perceived about God in the things that have been made, so that people are without excuse?
options: His invisible attributes, namely, his eternal power and divine nature
His complete plan of salvation in Christ Jesus
The demands of the moral law written on their hearts
His love and mercy toward all human beings
questions.correctAnswer: His invisible attributes, namely, his eternal power and divine nature
questions.explanation: Romans 1:20 (ESV): "For his invisible attributes, namely, his eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly perceived, ever since the creation of the world, in the things that have been made. So they are without excuse."

questions.question: Although they knew God, they did not honor him as God or give thanks to him, but they became futile in their thinking, and what happened to their foolish hearts?
options: They were darkened
They were hardened
They turned to stone
They became corrupt
questions.explanation: Romans 1:21 (ESV): "For although they knew God, they did not honor him as God or give thanks to him, but they became futile in their thinking, and their foolish hearts were darkened."

questions.question: Claiming to be wise, they became fools, and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for what?
options: Images resembling mortal man and birds and animals and creeping things
The wealth and power of this present world
The philosophies and traditions of human origin
The desires of the flesh and the deceitfulness of sin
questions.correctAnswer: Images resembling mortal man and birds and animals and creeping things
questions.explanation: Romans 1:22-23 (ESV): "Claiming to be wise, they became fools, and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images resembling mortal man and birds and animals and creeping things."

questions.question: Because they exchanged the truth about God for a lie and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, what did God do?
options: God gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to impurity
God sent prophets to warn them of coming judgment
God destroyed them with fire from heaven
God blinded their eyes so they could no longer see the truth
questions.correctAnswer: God gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to impurity
questions.explanation: Romans 1:24 (ESV): "Therefore God gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to impurity, to the dishonoring of their bodies among themselves,"

questions.question: Since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, God gave them up to a debased mind to do what ought not to be done. They were filled with all manner of what?
options: Unrighteousness, evil, covetousness, malice
Idolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife
Lust, greed, anger, and pride
Deceit, theft, murder, and adultery
questions.explanation: Romans 1:28-29 (ESV): "And since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, God gave them up to a debased mind to do what ought not to be done. They were filled with all manner of unrighteousness, evil, covetousness, malice."

questions.question: Though those with debased minds know God's righteous decree that those who practice such things deserve to die, what do they do?
options: They not only do them but give approval to those who practice them
They hide their deeds in darkness to avoid detection
They mock the law of God publicly and without shame
They try to change the law to justify their actions
questions.correctAnswer: They not only do them but give approval to those who practice them
questions.explanation: Romans 1:32 (ESV): "Though they know God's righteous decree that those who practice such things deserve to die, they not only do them but give approval to those who practice them."

key_verse_text: For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
